text: Every Tuesday before noon Claire would receive her meal kit in a box. It would be cold and sweaty from the ice packs and she would take it and open it in her kitchen. She would pull out the bag of chicken or kale or sesame oil. There would be little recipe cards in the box. She would read the instructions that say chop this, saute that, add, mix, etc. Obviously written for two people, to make the dish together. And she would cook it. She would sear the chicken and brush it with the sauce. The little apartment would smell incredible of ginger and clove. She would make rice and garnish it with scallions and sit there and eat. And it would almost feel like home. But then she would return the other plate and she would eat alone. But she always lays out two plates, always. For some reason. But it's different than cooking for someone who's going to eat and then want more. And then she would wash the little plastic containers that the food comes in and stack them up. And she would put the recipe card on the fridge with a little strawberry magnet. And maybe the next one would be lemon and thyme. But she didn't trust herself with that one yet but she would leave it up there.
